questions.scenario: The checkout application already calls `inventory.store.svc.cluster.local` through a Kubernetes Service. The platform enables an Istio sidecar mesh for the `store` namespace. What should application developers normally expect about that destination contract?

options.text: The application keeps calling the Kubernetes Service name while proxies intercept the request path around the application containers.
The application must replace every Service name with the private IP address of its local sidecar.
Kubernetes Services stop selecting Pods because the mesh control plane becomes the scheduler.
The application must call `istiod` directly for every inventory request.

questions.explanation: The mesh adds a managed proxy layer to the request path, but Kubernetes Services and DNS continue to provide the normal application destination. The control plane distributes configuration rather than carrying each application request.

questions.scenario: A traffic rule appears stale on many checkout Pods, while individual requests flow through Envoy sidecars. Which two statements correctly separate the mesh planes during investigation?

options.text: The Envoy sidecars are part of the data plane because they handle live service traffic.
The Kubernetes scheduler is the mesh data plane because it chooses nodes for Pods.
`istiod` is part of the control plane because it distributes configuration to proxies.
The application database is the mesh control plane because it stores business state.

questions.explanation: Data-plane proxies handle requests. The control plane watches configuration and pushes it to those proxies, so broad configuration staleness points toward control-plane or proxy-sync evidence rather than application business data.

questions.scenario: Namespace `store` has just received label `istio-injection=enabled`, but its three application Pods still show `1/1` ready. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.text: The label affects admission of newly created Pods, so existing workloads need a controlled restart before sidecars can appear.
The label injects a proxy into every already-running Pod immediately without changing Pod identity.
A `1/1` Pod proves the mesh is active because the app container has become the proxy.
The namespace label replaces the need for an installed mesh control plane.

questions.explanation: Sidecar injection happens when a Pod is admitted. Labeling a namespace makes future Pods eligible, so workloads must be restarted or rolled out, then verified for an application container plus a ready proxy.

questions.scenario: A store has fifteen services written in four languages. Each team has implemented different retry limits, identity checks, and request metrics for service-to-service calls. Which two repeated concerns are reasonable candidates for a centrally operated mesh layer?

options.text: Business rules that calculate customer discounts.
Consistent workload identity and mutual TLS between selected services.
Database schema migrations owned by each application.
Bounded traffic policy and proxy-level telemetry applied across languages.

questions.explanation: A mesh targets repeated communication concerns around traffic, identity, security, and telemetry. Application business rules and database migrations remain application responsibilities.

questions.scenario: A platform proposal describes a mesh as free reliability because applications do not change source code. Before production approval, which missing cost should reviewers insist on evaluating?

options.text: Only the number of characters in the mesh product name.
Proxy CPU and memory, request latency, control-plane availability, certificate rotation, upgrades, and new debugging paths.
Whether Kubernetes Services can be deleted after mesh installation.
Whether every business operation can move into the proxy configuration.

questions.explanation: The mesh adds infrastructure and failure modes even when application call sites stay unchanged. Production adoption needs capacity, latency, control-plane, identity, upgrade, and troubleshooting ownership.
